    Description
    AnnotationTargetUtils
    Resolves Target metadata for annotations represented by the Sourcegen model.
    BridgeResolver
    Resolves generic bridges from Sourcegen model, reflection, and annotation-processing types.
    BridgeResolver.Bridge
    A finished bridge method.
    BridgeResolver.BridgeMethod
    The erased method shape used by a bridge.
    BridgeResolver.InheritedBridge
    A bridge a class declares for a method it inherits.
    BridgeResolver.VisibilityBridge
    A visibility bridge: a public method a public class inherits from a superclass that is not public, which javac declares again in the class, delegating to the superclass's, so that reflection can invoke it through the class.
    ConstructorBody
    The body of a constructor as both bytecode writers write it: the constructor call first, then the initializers of the instance fields, then the rest of the statements.
    ConstructorBody.InitializersAfterThis
    Whether the field initializers run after a delegation to this(...).
    Conversions
    The conversions both bytecode writers emit, planned once as the steps each writer only emits: a checkcast, an unboxing with the source's wrapper, a primitive conversion and a boxing - Conversions.plan(TypeDef, TypeDef, ObjectDef, MethodDef, Conversions.Checkcasts).
    Conversions.Box
    A boxing of a primitive: the valueOf of its wrapper.
    Conversions.CheckCast
    A checkcast of a reference.
    Conversions.Checkcasts
    Which checkcasts of a conversion are left out as redundant.
    Conversions.PrimitiveConversion
    A conversion of a primitive to another: i2l, l2i followed by i2b, and so on.
    Conversions.Step
    A step of a conversion, which a writer emits as its instructions.
    Conversions.Unboxing
    An unboxing: a checkcast of the reference to the owner, which the method is invoked on, returning the primitive the owner holds, and a conversion of that primitive to the target, where it is another.
    DeclaredReturns
    The return type a class file declares for an invoked method, where the call names another: a T get() of a Getter<String> invoked for a String is written, as javac writes it, with the descriptor of its declaration, ()Ljava/lang/Object;, and a checkcast of the result.
    EnclosingScope
    The variables of the enclosing class in scope of the inner class a writer writes - a member class that is not static - of the generated class the outer type names: Supplier<T> of an inner class of an Outer<T> names the T of Outer.
    EnumGenUtils
    Model-level enum member synthesis shared by bytecode backends.
    InvocationPlan
    An invocation as both bytecode writers emit it, planned once: the instruction and what it names - the owner, the descriptor with the return type the method declares, whether the owner is an interface - what happens to the receiver, the parameters the arguments are converted to, and the conversion of the result to the type the call requests.
    InvocationPlan.Kind
    An invocation instruction.
    InvocationPlan.Receiver
    What happens to the receiver of an invocation once it is written.
    InvocationPlan.ResultConversion
    The conversion of what a declaration returns to the type the call requests.
    ModifierUtils
    Maps Java model modifiers to JVMS access flags without depending on a bytecode library.
    ReferenceAdapters
    The method references a metafactory cannot link to their method directly, which are written as a lambda calling it.
    ReferenceComparisons
    The referential comparisons (== and !=) of two primitives, which both bytecode writers compare as javac compares them: the values, promoted to a common type (JLS 5.6, binary numeric promotion) - a long compared with a float is compared as a float, and a char with a byte as an int.
    ReferenceComparisons.PrimitiveComparison
    Two primitive operands compared as their values: each one is written, then converted to the common type.
    SignatureUtils
    JVM generic-signature operations shared by bytecode writers.
    SwitchKeys
    The switches both bytecode writers write as a switch on an int, as javac writes them: a selector of type int, char, short or byte is widened to an int, and one of their wrappers is unboxed first, which throws NullPointerException for null.
    TypeUtils
    JVM descriptor operations shared by bytecode writers.
    TypeUtils.Receiver
    The type a call's receiver is written as.
